oewn-01062366-v.learner: to give someone something such as a compliment, your regards, or your attention.
examples: if Darcy were not such a great tall fellow, in comparison with myself, I should not pay him half so much deference
he thought of paying his addresses to one of her younger girls

oewn-02493705-v.learner: to make or carry out something, such as a visit.
examples: till the evening after the visit was paid she had no knowledge of it

oewn-02257962-v.learner: to clear something you owe, such as a debt, by settling it.
examples: His debts are to be paid, amounting, I believe, to considerably more than a thousand pounds

oewn-04681322-n.learner: the way a person or thing looks on the outside.
examples: a young man, whom they had never seen before, of most gentlemanlike appearance

oewn-07336372-n.learner: the moment when someone or something comes into sight.
examples: so abrupt was his appearance, that it was impossible to avoid his sight

oewn-00756620-n.learner: the act of pretending that something is so, in order to make a good impression.
examples: he is wise enough to assume even the appearance of what is right

connotation.why: presents the thing as put on rather than genuine

oewn-00491099-a.learner: happening, met with, or seen often, or following the regular way of doing things.
examples: there is something insufferably tedious in the usual process of such a meeting
pursue the usual course of their employments
the two gentlemen came directly towards them, and began the usual civilities

oewn-02153218-v.learner: to put something before people who want to see it.
examples: The picture gallery, and two or three of the principal bed-rooms, were all that remained to be shown.

oewn-02141597-v.learner: to let something be seen or noticed.
examples: she had never yet had courage to show Mrs. Gardiner's letter

oewn-00945869-v.learner: to give a feeling or thought an outward form.
examples: she saw how much affection and solicitude they showed for Jane

oewn-00666706-v.learner: to prove that something holds true, by an example, an explanation, or a test.
examples: He showed by a simple example that the rule always holds.

oewn-01944611-a.learner: fully what it is called, and deserving that name.
examples: where there is a real superiority of mind
he certainly would not marry Lydia, if he had not a real regard for her

oewn-02470192-s.learner: showing the true, inner nature of a person or thing.
examples: a person so well able to expose my real character
As to his real character, had information been in her power, she had never felt a wish of inquiring.

oewn-01939402-a.learner: existing in fact, with an existence that can be checked, and not a trick of the mind.
examples: The children wanted to know whether dragons were real animals.

oewn-02644022-v.learner: to stay in one place while you expect something to happen.
examples: Elizabeth, as they waited for the housekeeper, had leisure to wonder at her being where she was

oewn-02647547-v.learner: to hold back from doing something until later.
examples: it would be much better to wait till Jane was well

oewn-00721987-v.learner: to look ahead to something that is likely to happen.
examples: She waited news of the ship, which was due any day now.

oewn-07591291-n.learner: the largest meal of the day, eaten in the evening or in the middle of the day.
examples: at half-past six Elizabeth was summoned to dinner
The dinner was as well dressed as any I ever saw.

oewn-08270736-n.learner: a group of people gathered together to eat dinner.
examples: They gave a dinner for twenty guests on Thursday.

oewn-00028558-v.learner: to change the look on your face by spreading your lips, often to show that you are pleased.
examples: She smiled when she saw who was standing at the door.

oewn-01069534-v.learner: to say or show something by means of a smile.
examples: He smiled his thanks and went out.
She smiled her approval across the table.

oewn-04552265-n.learner: a path kept for people to walk along.
examples: leading the way through every walk and cross walk
She was proceeding directly to her favourite walk

oewn-00285642-n.learner: an occasion of walking to some place.
examples: Mr. Gardiner expressed a wish of going round the whole park, but feared it might be beyond a walk.
She took a walk in the garden before breakfast.

oewn-00284412-n.learner: the act of getting from place to place on foot.
examples: Within a short walk of Longbourn lived a family with whom the Bennets were particularly intimate.
The village lies an hour's walk from the house.

oewn-01584458-a.learner: needed so much that you cannot do without it.
examples: he took the opportunity of paying the parting civilities which he deemed indispensably necessary
That the Miss Lucases and the Miss Bennets should meet to talk over a ball was absolutely necessary

oewn-00344451-s.learner: bound to follow, because of what has already happened.
examples: Disgrace was the necessary result of such careless conduct.
